scope: Fix rejected native storage URLs, recover missing previews through originals, and prevent layout exceptions when rotating during reader entry

fixes.finding: Native photos retain a rejected storage URL after navigation
fixes.change: Reuse healthy URL metadata until its lifetime expires. Renew a failed storage download once automatically on native clients; share concurrent resolution/renewal and preserve an independently refreshed URL when an older failure arrives. Keep explicit retry usable after permanent failures.
verified: Previously decoded pixels are evicted, the old URL is rejected, and native route reentry renews it and displays the photo
Concurrent visible photos and reader preparation join the same pending download/renewal and use the same decode key
Permanent failure stops after the initial request plus one renewal; a later user retry can recover
Healthy URLs, token expiry, LRU eviction, pressure cleanup and failed-version invalidation behave correctly
A signing failure after its view leaves has no unhandled error
Late resolution cannot replace a different newly selected photo
Existing web manual retry and custom placeholder/error behavior remain covered

fixes.finding: An unavailable preview masks an accessible original
fixes.change: Share a normalized, deduplicated preview/image/original candidate order between visible photos and reader preparation. Retain only source-choice metadata, defer recent failed candidates without discarding them, and preserve the existing viewport decode bounds. Ensure custom artwork uses the same resized provider key as preparation; remove redundant resizing at the affected cover renderers.
verified: A main album cover displays its valid original after a missing preview
Reader preparation completes through the valid original and retains the same provider used by painting
Preparing while an original is downloading does not re-request a known-failed preview
Eight close/reopen visits reuse the working fallback, with live/pending image entries released after unmount and decoded cache within the test budget
If a remembered original fails on a later visit, a repaired preview remains available as an alternative
Closing during a pending fallback cannot start the remaining candidate
Bundled-asset alternatives recover remote previews with the requested decode dimensions
Original print rendering and crop-resolution requirements remain unchanged

fixes.finding: Reader entry rotation mutates AnimatedSize during its own layout
fixes.change: Remove the redundant AnimatedSize around the already-sized book stage. The opening overlay still interpolates entry geometry; book turns keep their existing renderer. Rotation applies the new viewport geometry directly and the book subtree stays mounted through entry handoff and reduced-motion changes.
verified: The original home-to-reader opening rotation regression now passes
An independent reader-only rotation while the opening overlay is active produces no layout exception
Entry handoff and reduced-motion changes preserve the same already-prepared BookFlip element
Page turning, cancellation, reverse turns, rapid picker changes, rotation and disposal tests pass
Moving covers land at the expected reader geometry across cover ratios and orientations

related_suite.scope: Home, collection, opening geometry, cover depth, reader photos, page turns, storage recovery, URL metadata, lifecycle, template previews, editor crop context and print crop resolution

verification.code_review: No additional blocking finding after reviewing retry bounds, candidate preservation, stale-response guards, provider key matching, closure ownership, cache cleanup and renderer handoff

limits: Network behavior was verified with in-memory download/signing fixtures and real Flutter image decoding. Existing HTTP/native calls may finish after a route is removed, but closed views do not apply their result or start another fallback. The metadata caches retain no image bytes, widgets or renderers; decoded pixels remain owned by Flutter's existing image cache. Test cache budgets and resource-release assertions do not constitute a measurement of total device memory or frame time.
